items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

Hello everyone! Since Aniimo launched, we’ve been blown away by your love and support. Thank you so much for stepping into Idyll and setting out on this adventure with us. Every hour you play and every kind word you share is what motivates us to keep going.

At the same time, we’ve seen plenty of honest feedback and complaints. Every suggestion, complaint, and question you post on social media, in comment sections, and in community is read and reviewed by our dev team. To us, such feedback shows that you genuinely love Aniimo and want it to get better.

Every so often, we’ll round up the issues you care about and talk about most, and share with you what we think, what we’re changing, and what’s coming next. Here are the top issues this time, along with our progress and plans:

1. Rerolling the same Aniimo keeps giving repeat colors and burns through resources. Can this be improved?

In version 1.1, we’re improving Sparkling Hue rerolls for Sparkling Prismana Aniimo. Once it’s live, you’ll be able to freely switch between any Sparkling Hue you’ve already unlocked for an Aniimo.

2. Some Aniimo already look great in their original Prismana colors. After using a Sparkling Cube, can I keep the original color?

After the version 1.1 update, you’ll be able to switch between all the Sparkling Hue styles unlocked for that Prismana Aniimo, including its original Prismana Hue, so you can switch back any time.

3. Why does my Legendary Irisalis have 88 Potential when someone else’s has 99?

We’ve read through all your feedback. Right now, Irisalis’s Innate Potential is random. Since you can only get this Legendary Aniimo once, having random Potential means the payoff isn’t guaranteed for this rare Aniimo. That’s not the experience we want for you.

So after the version 1.1 update, we’re removing Irisalis’s random Innate Potential and setting it to fixed values: ATK: 10, REGEN: 10, HP: 5, BREAK: 5, M.DEF: 5, P.DEF: 5

Any existing Potential above these values will be converted into Starcryst Essence as compensation. Watch for the version update announcement and in-game mail for the exact conversion rules and amounts.

4. Can I switch a Sparkling Aniimo I already own to a Legendary Aniipod’s exclusive Sparkling effect?

After the version 1.1 update, Legendary Aniipods can be used on Sparkling Aniimo. This replaces the Aniipod it was originally caught with and grants that Legendary Aniipod’s exclusive Sparkling effect.

5. Are there plans to fix lag and overheating on mobile?

We’ve received a lot of feedback on this. A dedicated team is optimizing for popular devices right now to reduce lag and overheating and improve the mobile experience as soon as possible.

6. Support tickets take a long time to get a reply. Can this be faster?

We’re continuing to improve how support works, including upgrading the support system, growing the team, and streamlining internal handoffs so that tickets get answered and resolved faster. Some complex issues require checking account data and working across several teams to find the cause, so they may take longer, but we’ll keep improving. Thank you for your patience and understanding.

7. My Steam/Console account failed to link. What should I do?

Please log in to our Customer Support page.

Under Quick Support Links, click Account Issues. Then select Steam Relink (PSN/Xbox) for both the second-level and third-level categories.

Please submit a support ticket with the following information:

- The platform ID you would like to unlink (e.g., Steam ID)

- The UID you are currently using to contact Customer Support, along with the email address linked to it

- The UID you would like to unlink

- The platform currently linked to the UID you would like to unlink

We will review your request and process it as soon as possible.

We’ll keep reviewing your real experiences and suggestions, and share bug fixes, improvements, mechanic changes, and future plans openly. We’d love to hear more of your feedback, too.

Thank you again to every Pathfinder for your patience and honest feedback. Every message you leave motivates us to keep improving. Have fun and enjoy your time in Idyll!

The Aniimo Dev Team

Seeing the World Through the Eyes of Monsters: How 'Aniimo' Expanded the Joy of Collection

items.content:
The Development Intent Behind 'Twine', Bridging Combat, Exploration, and Bonds

Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ▲ Aniimo - Global Official Launch Trailer ©Pawprint Studio The fun of discovering, capturing, and adventuring alongside monsters has now established itself as a full-fledged genre. Open-world creature-catching RPG 'Aniimo', officially launched on September 16, also begins from this familiar enjoyment, but presents a slightly different direction in how players connect with their companions. Beyond merely bringing Aniimo along, the game leads with the 'Twine' system, allowing players to directly become Aniimo and explore the world. Experiencing the world through the eyes and ears of the companions who fight beside you is the key differentiator this game puts forward.

This direction is also reflected in the overall game design, which connects combat, exploration, and collection. An Aniimo's elemental attribute extends beyond combat advantages to serve as a means of overcoming obstacles during exploration, while catching supports various approaches beyond reducing health, such as stealth and ambush. Ecological environments that shift with weather and time of day, along with branching evolution paths, add to the fun of getting to know each Aniimo. On top of this, the game packs content where players can stay long and enjoy time with their collected companions—ranging from competing against other players in 'Egg Heist' to decorating spaces with friends in 'Camper RV Camp'.

So, what kind of experience does 'Aniimo' aim to create to carve out its own place among numerous competitors? What was the reason behind binding combat, exploration, and bonds into a single system, and what thought went into helping players find their own fun amidst such a wide spectrum of content? Following the PC and console launch on September 16 and the mobile release on September 23, we sat down with the Design Director of 'Aniimo' to discuss the development intentions behind key systems and the direction of future updates.

The open-world creature-catching genre already has several competitors. If you had to pick one differentiator that only 'Aniimo' can offer within this genre, what would it be?

What was the reason behind deciding on a simultaneous release across various platforms such as Steam, Epic, Xbox, and PS5?

The core system of Aniimo, 'Twine', is impressive. It appears to encompass bonding, combat, and exploration altogether. What was the reason for binding these three elements into a single system?

Did you start development with the 'Twine' system set as the core pillar right from the early stages?

There are reviews noting that the combat system and skill structure are relatively simple. Was this simplicity intentionally designed?

There are as many as 9 elemental attributes for Aniimo. We are curious whether they are used solely for combat advantages and disadvantages (type matchups), or if feature-specific traits players can directly feel (exploration methods, field interactions, etc.) were also designed.

Monster-catching games usually follow a standardized formula of whittling down a monster's health and using a catching item. How does Aniimo's catching system differentiate itself from this traditional formula?

Around what events and conflicts does the main story unfold?

The way small-scale episodes named 'Journeys' appear unannounced was impressive. Was this designed for players to find them intentionally or by chance? Or is there a possibility of adjustments later for accessibility?

The vast and magnificent world is also impressive. When players first step foot onto the continent of Idyll, what impression did you want them to receive?

items.content:
Aniimo is a game that has multiple types of currencies that you can earn as you play the game. These currencies give you access to certain rewards and special items, but it can be difficult to know what currencies do, how important they are, and which ones you should be saving up. We have you covered. Here's everything you need to know about every currency that you can find while playing Aniimo.

Here are the major currencies that you'll be trying to unlock and add to your character as you play through Aniimo.

There are a lot of currencies for you to collect and keep track of while you play Aniimo. The premium currency is Lumin Crystals: they require real-world money to acquire and use, and there are few, if any, chances for you to unlock them by playing the game.

You primarily want to keep track of Credits, Glimmer, Home Coins, Starwish Coins, Voxel Coins , and Windborn Stamps.

Credits and Glimmer are readily available to you as you play the game, and are the standard currencies that you can acquire regularly by completing quests and story progression. Of the two, Glimmer is far more important, as you can use it at the in-game shop to purchase fruits, Aniipod Ultras, Redesign cards, or Primergy for in-game activities.

Home Coins are a currency you can get to unlock special furniture and items for your RV.

You can get Starwish Coins by turning in your Voxel Coins at the Super Lucky Star vendor, and you can only get 1,000 Voxel Coins per week. You want to unlock at least 1,000 once per week to make sure you can maximize this limited currency.

Finally, Windborn Stamps are available to you by completing various activities, and unlocking rewards in the Stamp Shop. These are limited to each season with Aniimo, and are important to redeem if you want those rewards for that season in the Companion Handbook.

10. Upgraded Voice-to-Text translation: detecting foreign speech now automatically transcribes and translates it into your language.

11. Enhanced interactive messaging: tapping a Pathfinder's avatar now directly opens their interaction panel.

12. Extended the bloom duration of Blooms from 2 minutes to 3 minutes.

13. Increased the single-purchase quantity limit in the Shop from 99 to 100.

Performance & Bug Fixes

1. Fixed an issue causing screen discoloration (red tinting) on certain devices.

2. Fixed localized rendering blackouts occurring on specific GPU models.

3. Resolved an issue where the client could enter an infinite reconnection loop under certain circumstances.

4. Optimized rendering performance for target-locking indicators and floating damage numbers.

5. Reduced UI-related stuttering for a smoother navigation experience.

6. Optimized memory management and performance overhead for select environmental assets.

7. Slightly increased the animation frame rate on PC.

Console/Controller-Specific Experience Optimization

1. Optimized combo key operations to prevent accidentally opening the emote bar during combat.

2. Added an operation tip "Long-press Y to open the radial menu" to the Settings system.

3. Adjusted some buttons in the event interface to trigger on long press.

4. Adjusted the "Nurture" button to trigger on tap.

5. Adjusted the help system pop-up to be entered by long-pressing the Option button.

6. Optimized the alignment display of quest bar icons and button prompts.

7. Fixed an issue where players could not navigate to the skin selection option when using a controller.

8. Fixed an issue where gradient colors could not be selected in the appearance interface.

9. Fixed an issue where the soft keyboard could not be brought up when entering a face customization code.

10. Fixed an issue where the soft keyboard could not be brought up when naming the "RV", and the name could not be changed when first seeing the Home RV.

11. Fixed an issue where the game incorrectly prompted that the controller was disconnected and the prompt window could not be closed.

12. Fixed an audio abnormality after returning to the game using Quick Resume.

13. Fixed an issue where Aniimo custom videos did not play on PS5.

14. Fixed an issue on Xbox where the game froze when opening the chat interface and sending text messages.

Other Experience Optimizations

1. The "Inherit" button is prominently displayed in the info interface for Pathfinders' convenience.

2. Optimized the icons and descriptions of Elite Training Plan Bonded Held Items.

3. Optimized the feedback prompt when Pathfinders' "Windborn Stamp" and "Voxel Coin" reach the acquisition cap.

>Bug Fixes

1. Fixed an issue where the core effect of the held item "Echoing Grimoire" triggered abnormally, so that the actual effect is consistent with the description.

2. Fixed an issue where the "Helion" model rarely disappeared in story cutscenes.

3. Fixed an issue in the journey quest "A Fragrant Dream" where two interactions were required to complete the quest.

4. Fixed an issue in "Pathfinder Challenge" where damage loss occasionally occurred after knocking enemies airborne.

5. Fixed an issue in "Pathfinder Challenge" where players were occasionally knocked outside the invisible wall.

6. Fixed an issue in "Pathfinder Challenge" where the invisible wall occasionally did not disappear.

7. Fixed an issue in "Pathfinder Challenge" where some Aniimo owners' names were incorrect.

8. Fixed an issue with abnormal model display for "Helmut".

9. Fixed an issue with abnormal model display for "Flamerion" after being revived from the fainted state.

10. Fixed an issue where, after "Blazen" entered the Overcharged state, switching to another Aniimo to release skills could not restore Ultimate Points.

11. Fixed an issue where players occasionally got stuck inside walls when entering and exiting climbing.

12. Fixed an issue in "Twine Mode" where sprinting on the beach did not leave footprints.

13. Fixed an issue where abnormal actions occurred after opening the "Menu" while the character was in the fainted state.

14. Fixed an issue in the "Sanctum" where restarting the client during the black screen of character fainting caused the character to get stuck.

15. Fixed an issue where screen flickering could occur when skipping story.

16. Fixed an issue where level 10 orders were incorrectly generated at "Home" level 9; order levels now correctly match "Home" level.

items.title: Free-to-play Creature Collector RPG Aniimo launches on PC, PlayStation, and Xbox
items.summary: Pawprint Studio has released creature collecting RPG, Aniimo, on PC (Steam, Epic), PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S.
items.content:
After months of beta testing, Pawprint Studio has released creature collecting RPG, Aniimo , on PC (Steam, Epic), PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. It’s also coming to mobile platforms on September 23.

Xbox Game Pass subscribers also receive an exclusive monthly Aniimo pack, which includes 1 Aniipod Ultra, 15 Growth Flowers, and 300 Glimmer.

Aniimo is a colorful world filled with creatures, inspired by Genshin Impact and Pokémon. As new Pathfinders, it’s the player’s job to explore the world of Idyll and discover the titular Aniimo.

At launch, the game includes over 200 Aniimo, including regional and color variants, and multiple rarities.

The open world features multiple territories supporting different levels of play, from quests to bosses and hidden treasures, and more.

In addition to summoning different Aniimo in real-time battle, players can also merge with their Aniimo directly. The process is called Twining, and it’s what sets Aniimo apart from most creature battlers. Through Twining, players become their favorite Aniimo, battling in third-person action. Each Aniimo has unique abilities and traits, and many can help travel around the world by gliding, climbing, or swimming.

Pathfinders also gain access to their own personal Homeland area, where they can build, expand, and customize an automated farm, and provide a home to their Aniimo.

I quite enjoyed the game when I played the Aniimo beta earlier this year.

Although primarily designed as an online single-player game (like many Hoyoverse gacha games ), Aniimo supports cooperative play to join with friends, or engage in specific PvP modes.

“The Aniimo team has worked diligently to finally bring the dreams of ourselves and our players to reality,” said Janson Zhang, Lead Game Designer, Pawprint Studio. “Through their efforts and immense support from Pathfinders around the globe, the world of Aniimo is now ready for you to discover with us, and we can’t wait to go on this journey together!”

New players can unlock the following free in-game launch rewards:

Aniimo is free-to-play on PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. It releases on September 23 on iOS and Android mobile platforms. A Mac version is also coming soon. It’s rated E10+.

items.title: Cute Critters Come to the Cloud: ‘Aniimo’ Launches on GeForce NOW
items.summary: Explore the creature-catching adventure at launch, alongside ‘Active Matter,’ ‘Outer Wilds’ and '007 First Light' with a path-tracing update.
items.content:
A new creature-catching adventure is ready to stream from the cloud this week. Pawprint Studio’s Aniimo arrives on GeForce NOW at launch, inviting gamers to explore the vibrant continent of Idyll across supported devices.

Also this week, 007 First Light receives a path-tracing update on GeForce NOW, alongside a smashing limited-time Deluxe Edition sale on Steam and Epic Games Store .

Gaijin Network’s fractured-multiverse action game Active Matter and Annapurna Interactive’s acclaimed space mystery Outer Wilds are also among 11 new titles joining the cloud this week.

The path to Idyll begins now. Aniimo is a free-to-play, open-world creature-catching role-playing game where every creature encountered can become a companion. Catch Aniimo with Aniipods, then Twine with them to take on their form and use unique skills to solve puzzles, win battles and overcome challenges.

Glide, dive and burrow across Idyll, then return to a personal RV to build a warm, interactive Homeland alongside Aniimo companions. Stream Aniimo on a Steam Deck , in the newly supported Firefox browser and across any other supported devices — without waiting through its 45GB download or making room in local storage. There’s always room in the Homeland for one more Aniimo.

In the critically acclaimed, multimillion-selling 007 First Light , follow James Bond as a young, resourceful and sometimes reckless recruit in MI6’s training program, and discover a reimagined origin story of the world’s most famous spy. Incorporating IO Interactive’s signature stealth gameplay with world-class Bond action, players can embark on missions in breathtaking locations around the globe, drive iconic vehicles and dive into a cinematic adventure in pursuit of a rogue agent who’s always one step ahead.

Path tracing has now been added to 007 First Light , introducing extra-detailed lighting, shadows and reflections, making its levels and set pieces even more cinematic, immersive and realistic. And NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction ensures the fidelity, clarity and accuracy of these additions are at their absolute best.

Ultimate members can stream with GeForce RTX 5080-class performance, with up to 5K high dynamic range and cinematic-quality streaming. DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution and Dynamic Frame Generation accelerate frame rates and enhance image quality.

A limited-time opportunity awaits: the 007 First Light Deluxe Edition is on sale on Steam from Sept. 15-29 and on Epic Games Store from Sept. 3-18. The mission is on sale. The getaway car is in the cloud.

Gaijin’s Active Matter , a realistic military shooter set in a fractured multiverse, has launched on GeForce NOW. As an operative stuck in a time loop, join dangerous raids for loot or intense player vs. player battles.

Fight against rivals from other timelines, survive physics-breaking anomalies and try to stay alive. Harvest active matter, gather loot and extract to a safe place before the whole zone ceases to exist.

Ultimate members can take on each raid with GeForce RTX 5080-class performance in the cloud, delivering high frame rates, advanced graphics features and low latency across supported devices. The zone won’t wait — and neither does the next loop.

Outer Wilds joins the GeForce NOW library this week. As the newest recruit of Outer Wilds Ventures, search for answers across a strange, ever-changing solar system trapped in an endless time loop. Gamers can trace mysterious signals, decipher alien writing and discover hidden locations before an underground city is swallowed by sand or a planet crumbles beneath their feet.

Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after they’re released and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates to announced titles.

more ambitious with the launch of Aniimo , a free-to-play open-world RPG that lets you do more than simply capture and battle its colourful inhabitants.

Developed and published by Pawprint Studio, Aniimo is now available on Xbox Series X|S, PC and PlayStation 5, with Xbox Play Anywhere support included. The game is also available through Game Pass Day One across the Ultimate, Essential, Premium and PC tiers, while a mobile release is scheduled for September 23rd.

We first covered Aniimo back in 2025 , when its unusual Twining mechanic offered an early glimpse at how it planned to stand apart from other creature-collecting adventures.

Aniimo takes players to the expansive continent of Idyll, a world where creatures known as Aniimo can be found across a variety of environments. Their appearances and behaviours are influenced by factors such as weather, time of day and surrounding phenomena, giving exploration a purpose beyond simply travelling from one objective to the next.

Capturing these creatures requires a little more thought than pressing a button and moving on. Players can use Aniipods, set traps and carefully time their attempts, while the creatures themselves can evolve as their journey progresses.

The aim is to build a collection, but Aniimo also wants players to develop a connection with the creatures they discover.

The defining feature of Aniimo is its Twining system. Rather than simply sending a creature into battle, players can merge with their collected Aniimo and experience the world through their abilities and perspective.

This can open up new ways to approach puzzles, overcome obstacles and engage in battles. Depending on the creature involved, players may be able to glide, dive, burrow or use other skills to reach places that would otherwise remain inaccessible.

That makes the process of collecting Aniimo feel directly connected to exploration. Finding a new creature isn’t only about adding another entry to your collection – it could also provide the solution to a problem you’ve encountered elsewhere in Idyll.

Idyll isn’t intended to be explored entirely alone. Players can visit a floating metropolis, meet fellow Pathfinders and take part in competitive battles, while the PvEvP mode known as Egg Heist introduces a more immediate multiplayer challenge.

In Egg Heist, teams of three head into the Lost Isles to search, compete and battle in real time. The mode is designed to mix cooperation with uncertainty, ensuring that other players can complicate proceedings as you work towards your objective.

Outside of combat, each Pathfinder also has access to a personal RV parked at a campsite. This provides a place to interact with other players, while returning to Homeland allows you to plant crops, arrange decorations and customise your own space.

Aniimo is available now on Xbox Series X|S, PC and PlayStation 5, with Play Anywhere support on Xbox and PC thanks to the Xbox Store download. The mobile version follows on September 23rd.

DLSS or FSR Quality mode, depending on your GPU, is doing a lot of the heavy lifting here. It renders the game at a lower internal resolution and upscales the image back to 4K, clawing back a good chunk of performance without making things look soft. Keeping VSync off helps input lag stay low too, which matters even in a laid-back game like Aniimo.

DLSS Frame Generation lets you push the multiplier up to 6x or hand things over to Dynamic Mode. However, I have settled on 4x as the best balance, since going higher can introduce a bit of smearing around fast-moving creatures without adding much once your base frame rate is already solid. If you are using an extremely high refresh rate monitor and want the smoothest motion possible, try pushing it to 6x or testing Dynamic Mode to see how your setup feels.

You can keep all on High for Global Illumination, Reflection Quality, Ambient Occlusion, and Shadow Quality, since a high-end PC can handle real-time lighting without breaking a sweat. Bake Global Illumination is left off on purpose, as it swaps in a static, pre-computed lighting solution meant for lower-end GPUs.
